## Who won prizes at the Berlinale 2024?
**Golden Bear for Best Film:** _Dahomey_ by Mati Diop, produced by Eve Robin, Judith Lou Lévy, Mati Diop
**Silver Bear, Grand Jury Prize** : _Yeohaengjaui pilyo (A Traveler’s Needs)_ , dir. Hong Sangsoo

**Silver** **Bear for Best Screenplay** : Matthias Glasner for _Dying_ , dir. Matthias Glasner

## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mati_Diop&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Diop was born in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"). Her father, [Wasis Diop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasis_Diop "Wasis Diop"), is a black Senegalese musician, while her mother, Christine Brossard, is a white French art buyer and photographer. She is the niece of filmmaker [Djibril Diop Mambéty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djibril_Diop_Mamb%C3%A9ty "Djibril Diop Mambéty"). During her childhood, she often travelled back and forth between France and Senegal, developing a transnational identity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-1)
## Education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mati_Diop&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Education")]
Diop trained in the Advanced Degree Programme at Le Fresnoy National Studio of Contemporary Art in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-2) as well as at the [Palais de Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_de_Tokyo "Palais de Tokyo") in their experimental artist studio space Le Pavillon.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-:0-3)
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mati_Diop&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]
Diop was a fellow at the [Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radcliffe_Institute_for_Advanced_Study "Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study") from 2014 to 2015.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-:0-3) Her work there focused on themes of exile, identity, memory, and loss, utilizing both fiction and documentary techniques.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-4) While a part of the institute's selective Film Study Center Fellowship Program, she wrote the script for her first feature film _Fire, Next Time._[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_note-:0-3) She later changed the title of this film to what is now known as her directorial feature film debut, _[Atlantics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantics "Atlantics")_ (2019).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mati_Diop#cite_no
